faq.answer: No. The course introduces the concepts in a mechanical engineering friendly way.

faq.question: What will I learn beyond theory?
faq.answer: You will work through system logic, monitoring ideas, and application-based mechanical tasks.

faq.question: Is this aligned with Industry 4.0 trends?
faq.answer: Yes. The program is shaped around connected systems, automation, and digital modeling concepts.

tasks.title: Engine Heat Dissipation Script
tasks.assignment: Write a script to calculate heat dissipation on an engine block.
tasks.ai_review: The AI checks the syntax and evaluates whether the output values fall within the expected thermodynamic safety limits.

tasks.title: Toolpath Instruction Set
tasks.assignment: Write the toolpath instructions to mill a specific geometric part.
tasks.ai_review: The AI reads the coordinates to ensure the toolpath does not exceed the physical bounding box, which would cause a machine crash.

tasks.title: Steel Reorder Logic
tasks.assignment: Build a logic flow that automatically orders steel when inventory drops below 15%.
tasks.ai_review: The AI tests the inventory thresholds. If it triggers the order at 20% instead of 15%, it issues a correction.

tasks.title: Turbine RPM + Vibration Parsing
tasks.assignment: Parse live RPM and vibration data from a simulated turbine.
tasks.ai_review: The AI feeds dirty data into the script and checks whether the code successfully isolates the anomalies.

tasks.title: Robotic Line API + Halt Logic
tasks.submission: API logic flow document and automation design.
tasks.assignment: Design the API and logic flow for a robotic assembly line, including defect detection alerts and automated halting protocols.
tasks.ai_review: The AI pressure-tests the logic: if Robot A fails, does the student's script safely halt Robot B?
